caption: Follow the lysate into every printed spot: the address tracks sample and dilution, not a cell’s former tissue position. The dilution design is invented. Separate antibodies need their own specificity, calibration and normalization; the array is not an all-protein or single-cell spatial census.
alt: Invented cells from a defined specimen are disrupted into a tube containing mixed protein shapes. A printed array uses rows for samples A and B and columns for toy dilutions 1, one-half and one-quarter; every spot retains mixed protein symbols. Two replicate array layouts receive separate antibodies for R and phospho-R. Print addresses are sample/dilution labels rather than cell positions. Specificity, calibration and loading normalization remain assay-specific; this is not all-protein or single-cell spatial measurement.
